prpt6ty.s: Techno club beneath the Knockdown Center in Maspeth, Queens, opened in 2019. Funktion-One surround sound, a 360-degree light rig, no photos or video, and a safer-space policy. 21+.

p1oe878x.s: Huge open-air dance venue in the Avant Gardner complex in East Williamsburg. It has been closed since the company's 2025 bankruptcy, so check its status before planning a night.

p1jtdkw3.s: Indoor warehouse hall in the Avant Gardner complex in East Williamsburg, next to the Brooklyn Mirage. The complex went through bankruptcy in 2025, so check current listings.

p1ty5p0i.s: Greenpoint dance club that feels like a big, friendly warehouse party, with ticketed DJ nights and a disco ball. Time Out lists it as currently closed.

p1x5rnpb.s: Rooftop bar and dance floor on top of The Standard, High Line, with DJs, Hudson River views and a famous hot tub.

pl4oke6.s: Long-running DIY music and dance venue in Bushwick, upstairs on Myrtle Avenue beside the elevated train tracks.

pbvp9jg.s: Big-room Chelsea nightclub from the Tao Group, reopened after a major renovation, with headline DJs.

p10cpq48.s: Large dance-music club near Times Square that opened in late 2021.

puw7whe.s: Tiny Lower East Side club (about 140 people) for house and techno, with bottle service and a few vintage arcade games.

p11z1iw2.s: Rooftop lounge at the top of the Dream Downtown hotel in Chelsea.

p1ijanpi.s: Nightclub and performance space inside Ian Schrager's Public Hotel on Chrystie Street, pitched as downtown's answer to Studio 54.

p1cvtpnf.s: Brooklyn "hi-def dance club" built around an audiophile sound system, opened in 2025 by two veterans of New York nightlife.

psijtas.s: 500-capacity Brooklyn nightclub for electronic music that opened in February 2023.

p1pia2l.s: 210-capacity warehouse club in East Williamsburg with a strict no-phones dance floor; one of Brooklyn's buzziest new clubs in 2025.

pmpn09r.s: New York outpost of Silencio, the Paris club first designed by David Lynch. An exclusive, members-leaning space with surreal interiors by Harry Nuriev.

p5ki3l9.s: Rooftop lounge and club with a secret-garden look, a pool and 360-degree city views; billed as the highest club with a pool in NYC.

p1or6r1t.s: Three-level mid-size concert hall at 610 West 56th Street in Hell's Kitchen, a regular stop for touring bands and DJs.

p4z4ine.s: Late-night theater club on Freeman Alley on the Lower East Side, known for risqué, X-rated cabaret and burlesque shows.

p1ali21f.s: Williamsburg nightclub with a selective door (guests apply online) and a design by Studio MBM and Yakka Studio.

p2bfkh8.s: 3,000-square-foot club for house and electronic music on the Lower East Side waterfront.

p5q2jsx.s: Small, intimate karaoke bar in SoHo that also hosts private parties.

pgtro45.s: Little Greenpoint aperitivo bar inspired by the bars of Spain and northern Italy. Good for a date.

ppmssco.s: Lower East Side cocktail and oyster bar with live music and small bites. A classic first-date spot.

p7u5ehy.s: Apartment-style bar with live jazz, vinyl, Japanese whisky and creative cocktails. Moody, intimate and good for listening.

p1vfw0wc.s: Legendary piano bar in the Carlyle Hotel since the 1940s, wrapped in Ludwig Bemelmans' Madeline murals. White-jacketed service, live music and serious martinis.

p1ctfel9.s: Two-story Williamsburg spot: a casual cocktail bar upstairs and a club-like basement where you dance under a disco ball.

pc6fsca.s: Cocktail bar from the Eleven Madison Park team at 11 Madison Avenue, the easier way into that world.

p1n3yxe5.s: Immersive "modern conversation parlor" with elaborately themed rooms, cocktails and a no-phones rule, built to get strangers talking.

p1qv5g8c.s: East Village dive on Avenue A with a '90s punk attitude and a no-frills crowd.

pmivk7.s: 36-seat Greenpoint cocktail bar built for listening, with obscure records on a serious sound system.

puteip3.s: Wine bar on Great Jones Street from the team behind Le Dive. Chilled reds, artichokes and a sexy little room.

p9cjoxu.s: Faena's first New York hotel, opened in West Chelsea in September 2025, with murals, fire-cooked feasts, disco-ball altars and theatrical bars.

p1rqqdze.s: Intimate Williamsburg bar opened in late 2023 by DJ Eli Escobar and Rafael Ohayon, already full of regulars.

p5v4dos.s: Polished downtown lounge for late nights, with house music and a stylish crowd.

p1a7mpfe.s: Chelsea sushi spot with sets and a chef's omakase you usually can't get for delivery.

p1wbrujq.s: Speakeasy-style bar on Avenue C in Alphabet City that looks like a fancy 1970s living room.

plp8m1n.s: Lower East Side Mexican restaurant and dance club in a basement built to look like a cave, with tacos and hookah.

pze820h.s: Busy little wine bar on Canal Street in the middle of Dimes Square. Great for a drink, snacks and people-watching.

p17r73an.s: Closet-sized Chinatown wine bar with a 25-page wine list and creative Chinese-American small plates.

p1sdr61x.s: Cocktail bar in NoMad on West 28th Street, with its own street entrance.

p19zcray.s: Heavy-metal bar in Gowanus with bands in the back room and go-go dancers on the bar.

p1l94jj6.s: Cocktail bar from the team behind Frankie and the newer Cafe Binx in the West Village.

p143yth3.s: Williamsburg date bar with vinyl on the stereo and fries piled with tzatziki.

p4prpy5.s: Bar at 443 West 15th Street in West Chelsea, on a block known for late-night spots.

p18qyl4g.s: Ridgewood institution for day drinking and dancing, from the Mister Saturday Night crew, with a top-flight sound system and a laid-back crowd.
